paper_title: Probing the Blue Axion with Cosmic Optical Background Anisotropies
notes: Paper presents a NEW (recomputed/improved) exclusion limit on decaying axion-like dark matter (5-25 eV 'blue axion') from HST cosmic optical background anisotropy measurements at 606 nm, plus PROJECTIONS at 438/336 nm and for LIM (HETDEX). The primary results are shown as exclusion curves on the lifetime/decay-rate (Gamma_a->gg vs m_a) and coupling (g_agamma vs m_a) planes in Figs. 1, 8, 9, but no numerical tables are given. The only explicit numerical value of THEIR bound in the text is from the Note Added: at m_a = 4.2 eV, HST 606 nm excludes Gamma >= 3.03e-25 s^-1, corresponding to g_agamma >= 2.33e-11 GeV^-1 (emitted as the single data point). Other explicit numbers in text (HB: g<0.65e-10 GeV^-1; VIMOS: g<3e-12 for 4.5-7.7 eV; FIRAS) are pre-existing bounds from other works and were not included. This is a cosmological decaying-DM bound, not a haloscope, so no local DM density assumed. Full exclusion curve would require figure digitization; hence moderate extraction confidence. The likelihood-based bounds are at 95% CL. | selector: text over figure_vision (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0.5, 1))
